rounds.text: Apar Industries exhibits exceptional structural compounding power, evidenced by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 29% and a phenomenal profit growth of 44% [E15, E19]. This impressive operational performance is underpinned by elite returns on capital, featuring an extraordinary ROCE of 31.8% and a robust ROE of 20.3% [E12, E13], heavily outperforming sector benchmarks [E10, E9]. The growth runway remains wide open, propelled by a soaring conductor division pending order book of ₹10,190 crores with 56.8% in exports [E84], alongside massive multi-year overseas utility orders exceeding ₹2,800 crores [E90]. Institutional confidence is surging as domestic institutions expanded holdings by 5.21 percentage points and foreign institutions added 1.57 percentage points [E43, E42], signaling a POSITIVE MONEY FLOW institutional signal [E44]. To capture this surging demand, the company is aggressively expanding capacity, aggressively ramping up its FY27 capital expenditure plans to approximately ₹1,500 crores following ₹740 crores in FY26 [E79], while maintaining a conservatively financed balance sheet with a modest debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E37]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 52.5x and a rich price-to-book of 11.26x [E1, E2], accompanied by a discounted cash flow intrinsic valuation warning [E45] and an inconsistent short-term operating margin trend [E32].

Apar Industries trades at a lofty price-to-earnings ratio of 52.5x and a price-to-book multiple of 11.26x, both sitting well above sector benchmarks of 22.54x and 2.44x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This aggressive valuation leaves no room for error, especially when a discounted cash flow model values the company at ₹ 11,498 per share against a market price of ₹ 15,122, creating a negative margin of safety of -31.5% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the company's current stock price already bakes in an ambitious 21.8% earnings growth rate [E47], while price growth has substantially outpaced profit growth over the past five years [E56]. Conceded: the company boasts impressive historical compound sales growth of 29% over five years and strong returns on capital employed [E10, E15]. However, balance sheet and operational friction are mounting, evidenced by borrowings increasing to ₹ 956 Cr from ₹ 585 Cr [E39], capital work-in-progress spiking by 315.4% into a heavy capex cycle [E40], and recent promoter holdings slipping to 55.42% [E41]. External vulnerabilities also surfaced during the last quarter through volume contractions in both the conductor and oil divisions [E88, E89], alongside provisions of approximately ₹ 94 crores in the oil division stemming from extreme volatility in crude and gas oil prices [E81].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E6, E7, E45, E46, E47]. While these valuation multiples look elevated, they reflect a world-class operating efficiency that dwarfs sector medians, including an exceptional ROCE of 27.5% to 31.8% against a sector benchmark of just 12.93% and an ROE of 18.11% to 20.3% versus the sector's 10.85% [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. The rising borrowings to ₹ 956 Cr and the 315.4% surge in capital work-in-progress to ₹ 540 Cr are not operational distress signals, but rather the deliberate funding of an aggressive, high-return capex expansion—including a planned ₹ 1,500 Cr for FY27—aimed directly at capturing structural energy infrastructure demand [E39, E40, E77, E79]. Furthermore, the dip in promoter holding is entirely offset by surging institutional confidence, with foreign and domestic institutions increasing their stakes by 1.57 and 5.21 percentage points respectively, driving a "POSITIVE MONEY FLOW" signal [E41, E42, E43, E44]. Finally, the volume contractions cited in the oil and conductor divisions were temporary bumps driven by external shocks like the U.S.-Iran war and port closures, which did not prevent the conductor division from securing a massive pending order book of around ₹ 10,190 crores and generating higher absolute EBITDA per ton [E83, E84, E87, E89].

Conceded: [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. While those return metrics look robust, the bull glosses over the severe valuation disconnect where a discounted cash flow model values the stock at Rs 11,498 against a market price of Rs 15,122, leaving a negative margin of safety of -31.5% [E45, E46]. Furthermore, the bull characterizes the surging capex and borrowings of Rs 956 Cr up from Rs 585 Cr as unalloyed growth, ignoring that the reverse DCF indicates today's price already demands an aggressive 21.8% earnings growth that outpaces the base case [E39, E40, E47, E79]. The bull dismisses volume contractions as temporary external shocks, yet the record explicitly shows conductor volumes dropping 6.7% and oil volumes falling 13.7% due to volatile metal prices and port closures, alongside an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E32, E33, E88, E89]. While institutional ownership increased, promoter holdings actively declined by 2.35 percentage points over recent quarters, and the cost of borrowing has been flagged as a negative [E41, E42, E43, E61, E62]. Finally, chasing this price-led momentum ignores the historical risk of an 82.6% peak-to-trough drawdown when expectations run ahead of delivery [E53, E56, E57].

Conceded: [E45, E46]. While the DCF suggests a lower intrinsic value, the market price is heavily supported by a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E63] and institutional money flow registering as POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with foreign and domestic holdings expanding over time [E42, E43, E44]. The bear's concern over surging borrowings [E39] ignores the massive growth investments underway, including CWIP expanding by +315.4% [E40] and a planned FY27 capex of INR1,500 crores following INR740 crores in FY26 [E79], which directly feed stellar 5-year compounded sales growth of 29% and profit growth of 44% [E15, E19]. Conceded: [E32, E33, E88, E89]. Although volume contractions occurred due to volatile metal prices and port disruptions [E88, E89], absolute profitability expanded significantly, with conductor absolute EBITDA growing to INR53,418 per ton versus INR43,688 a year earlier [E83] and oil division EBITDA margins surging to INR25,482 per kL compared to INR7,004 [E82]. Furthermore, promoter holding adjustments [E41] pale against surging new order inflows from the US [E76], a massive conductor order book of around INR10,190 crores with 56.8% export backing [E84], and massive long-term multi-year utility orders exceeding ₹ 2,800 crores [E90].

Conceded: [E42, E43, E44, E82, E83, E84]. The bull's reliance on massive planned capital expenditure—scaling to ₹1,500 crores in FY27 after ₹740 crores in FY26 [E79] alongside a 315.4% surge in CWIP [E40]—actively underpins the bear's primary risk argument: borrowings have already escalated to ₹956 crores from ₹585 crores [E39], driving high borrowing costs [E62] against a thin current ratio buffer of 1.45x [E38]. While absolute per-unit margins expanded temporarily [E82, E83], volume metrics contracted visibly with conductor volumes down 6.7% due to metal price volatility [E88] and oil volumes dropping 13.7% from port disruptions in the UAE [E89], exposing the fragility of earnings when external shocks hit. Conceded: [E76, E79, E80, E90]. Despite these order book tailwinds, the stock trades at an extreme valuation of 52.5x P/E [E1] and 11.26x P/B [E2], heavily outstripping sector benchmarks of 22.54x and 2.44x [E6, E7] while insiders quietly pare their stakes down to 55.42% [E41]. Finally, pointing to backward-looking 5-year growth rates [E15, E19] ignores the reality that today's price sits at a severe -31.5% discount to DCF intrinsic value [E45, E46], demanding an unrealistic 21.8% future earnings growth just to justify the current multiple [E47].

evidence.fact: Management stated that the structural energy infrastructure fundamentals remain robust, supported by growth in T&D, rising electricity demand, and increasing evacuation infrastructure.
evidence.quote: However, having said that, structurally, energy infrastructure fundamentals remain intact with the growth in T&D, rising electricity demand and evacuation infrastructure being increased, data center expansion, the growing presence of EVs, more opportunities for reconducting and upgradation of aging lines and, finally, the significant investment happening in ultra-high voltage transmission infrastructure and HVDC.

evidence.fact: Management noted that the Middle East business will remain somewhat subdued until the ongoing war is resolved.
evidence.quote: So I see that the Middle East business will continue to remain a little bit subdued until this war gets completed.

evidence.fact: The company plans to increase its capital expenditure for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores, following an expenditure of INR740 crores in FY26.
evidence.quote: We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores.

evidence.fact: The planned capex breakup for FY27 includes around INR400 crores from the conductor division, around INR200-odd crores from the oil division, and approximately INR850 crores from the cable division.
evidence.quote: Around INR400 crores would be coming from conductor division, around INR200-odd crores on oil division, and cable would be in the range of INR850 crores.

evidence.fact: The company provided approximately INR94 crores for the oil division in the quarter in line with accounting standards due to sharp rises and falls in crude and gas oil prices.
evidence.quote: So, with the price of crude oil and gas oil having risen very sharply at the beginning of the quarter and then falling quite sharply at the end of the period, the company has followed the requirements of accounting standards and has provided for approximately INR94 crores for the oil division in the quarter.

evidence.fact: The oil division's EBITDA margins came in at a substantially higher level of INR25,482 per kL compared to INR7,004 per kL a year ago.
evidence.quote: However, post taking this provision into account, the EBITDA margins came in at a substantially higher level of INR25,482 per kL compared to INR7,004 per kL a year ago.

evidence.fact: Conductor division absolute EBITDA grew to INR53,418 per ton compared to INR43,688 per ton a year earlier.
evidence.quote: EBITDA growth is attributable to a higher share of the premium mix due to which despite a slightly lower volume of conventional conductors, the absolute EBITDA has grown, which came in at INR53,418 per ton compared to INR43,688 per ton a year earlier.

evidence.fact: The conductor division's pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%.
evidence.quote: The pending order book stands at around INR10,190 crores with an export proportion of 56.8%.

evidence.fact: New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, with exports contributing 65.8%.
evidence.quote: New orders received by the conductor division were INR5,245 crores in the quarter, of which exports contributed to 65.8%.

evidence.fact: The cable division's pending order stands at INR1,925 crores compared to INR1,653 crores from a year ago.
evidence.quote: The pending order today stands at INR1,925 crores. So it largely covers the plan or the requirement for the current -- for the coming quarter compared to INR1,653 crores from a year ago.

evidence.fact: The quarter was challenging due to the impact of the U.S.-Iran war, logistics difficulties in export markets, and manpower shortages in May.
evidence.quote: Otherwise, this has been a fairly challenging quarter from an external perspective, given the impact of the U.S.-Iran war, various logistics difficulties that have happened in the export markets and fairly significant manpower-related shortages in the month of May, which coincided with holidays as well as local elections.

evidence.fact: Conductor volumes were down 6.7% due to a surge in metal prices impacting delivery schedules where customers withheld manufacturing clearance.
evidence.quote: Volume for the quarter was down 6.7% compared to a year ago. This can be attributed fundamentally to a surge in the metal prices that have impacted delivery schedules of orders which are in hand, where customers have withheld manufacturing clearance, especially due to the sudden increase in the price of aluminum and where customers were not having hedged metal.

evidence.fact: Oil division volumes were affected because the UAE facility was restricted to making local deliveries due to the crisis and resulting closure of the Hamriyah port.
evidence.quote: Volume for the quarter stands at 129,085 kL, down 13.7% compared to a year ago and down -- yes, the volumes were affected really because of our facility in the UAE, which because of this crisis and the resulting closure of the Hamriyah port was restricted to only making local deliveries of the product that it had in inventory.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): Large orders exceeding ₹ 2,800 crores from two major overseas electric utility companies have a delivery period spread over the next 4 years.
evidence.quote: This includes large orders exceeding ₹ 2,800 crores from two major overseas electric utility companies with a delivery period spread over next 4 years reinforcing the investments behind transmission capex globally

evidence.fact: Management commitment: Management stated that from a medium to long-term perspective, conductor margins are expected to be in the range of INR35,000 to INR36,000 per metric ton plus tailwinds.
evidence.quote: And based on the historical EBITDA margin that we have made, we expect that from a medium to long-term perspective, our conductor margins could be in the range of INR35,000 to INR36,000 per metric ton.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company plans to increase its capital expenditure for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores.
evidence.quote: We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores.
